{
  "jobspec": "#!/bin/bash

# Flux batch script (translated from PBS)

# PBS requested:
#   -P CBBI1106
#   -N array_job
#   -l select=1:ncpus=24
#   -o /mnt/lustre/users/blombard/reinfectionsBelinda/oe_files/array_job_m1.out
#   -e /mnt/lustre/users/blombard/reinfectionsBelinda/oe_files/array_job_m1.err
#   -l walltime=1:00:00
#   -J 1-21:21   (job array)
#   -q smp
#   -M belindalombard@sun.ac.za
#   -m be

# This PBS script is an array job. Flux has no single universally portable array directive.
# Provide the array index via environment variable ARRAY_INDEX when submitting.
# Example: ARRAY_INDEX=1 flux batch <this_script>

flux alloc \
  -N 1 \
  -n 1 \
  -c 24 \
  --time=1h \
  --queue=smp \
  bash -lc '

# Approximate PBS stdout/stderr file directives
exec >"/mnt/lustre/users/blombard/reinfectionsBelinda/oe_files/array_job_m1.out" \
     2>"/mnt/lustre/users/blombard/reinfectionsBelinda/oe_files/array_job_m1.err"

# NOTE: PBS -P CBBI1106 (project/allocation) has no universally portable Flux batch directive.
# Performance implication: none for runtime, but accounting/charging/allocation association may be incorrect.

# NOTE: PBS email notifications (-M / -m) have no universally portable Flux batch directive.
# Performance implication: none for runtime, but you will not receive begin/end emails.

# NOTE: PBS -J 1-21:21 (array semantics) has no universally portable Flux batch directive.
# Performance implication: you lose scheduler-managed array handling; you must submit the desired indices yourself.

# NOTE: PBS -N array_job (job name) has no universally portable Flux batch directive.
# Performance implication: none (metadata only).

sleep 4

module add chpc/R/3.5.1-gcc7.2.0

cd /mnt/lustre/users/blombard/reinfectionsBelinda/

make sbv

STEP=21
: "${ARRAY_INDEX:?ARRAY_INDEX must be set (1..21 step 21) to replace PBS_ARRAY_INDEX}"
START=${ARRAY_INDEX}
END=$(( START + STEP - 1 ))

for i in $(eval echo "{$START..$END}")
do
	(echo "process $i started" && Rscript sbv/method_1_analysis/method_1_arrayjob.R $i && echo "process $i finished") &
done

sleep 0.1

echo "Waiting for processes to finish"
wait $(jobs -p)
echo "All processes finished"
'
"
}
